newsitem.title: USA: U.S. carbon steel imports in Nov were highest ever.
newsitem.headline: U.S. carbon steel imports in Nov were highest ever.

text.p: Imports of carbon steel into the United States in November 1996 were 3,155,401 net tons of steel mill products, the American Iron and Steel Institute reported.

"As indicated by recent petitions filed by U.S. member companies of AISI, there is reason to believe that an increasing number of imports are entering the U.S. market at dumped prices," the AISI added in a statement.
This is the highest level of imports for a single month ever, based on U.S. Commerce Department data, the AISI said.
November imports were up 12.4 percent from the 2,807,961 net tons imported in October 1996, and up 84.8 percent from the 1,707,466 net tons of steel in November 1995.
In January through November, the U.S. imported 26,626,322 net tons of steel mill products, up 16.9 percent from the same period last year.
November imports were 29.5 percent of apparent consumption, the highest figure since September 1985.

The sharpest increases in 1996 imports in January through November came from Europe (up 48 percent) Brazil (up 32.9 percent), Mexico (up 26.6 percent), Ukraine (up 23.6 percent) and, to a lesser extent, China (up 15.3 percent), and Canada (up 8.1 percent).
Imports from Turkey plunged 35.6 percent and down 19.7 percent from Japan.
The U.S. exported 361,934 net tons of mill products in November, down 12.8 percent from October 1996, and down 42.2 percent from November 1995.
Exports in Jan through Nov were down 27.2 percent to 4,657,147 tons.
